name: CEPI (Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations): charityevals' estimate
beneficiaries_note: Our build: a pandemic kills people everywhere and the future lost is everyone's, so the result is spread by world population; the endemic branch (Lassa, mpox, chikungunya) is under 1% of the result and left in the world figure.
summary: CEPI (Oslo) funds vaccines against epidemic and pandemic threats: rapid-response platforms and vaccine libraries for an unknown virus, vaccines against Lassa, Nipah, mpox, chikungunya, Rift Valley fever, filoviruses and coronaviruses, manufacturing in the Global South and the tools behind its 100 Days Mission. This model of all its work in 2025 (its latest audited accounts, $449M) comes to about {{result}} years of healthy life per $1,000, from 0.02 to 13 on the combined range: each dollar is valued as a typical pandemic project's cut in the forecast risk (Rethink Priorities' cross-cause model, the Existential Risk Persuasion Tournament's experts), measured at CEPI's size by the 100 Days Mission's own estimate of its worth, about 7% of a typical project's rate; the vaccines' use against today's outbreaks adds under 1%. The biggest uncertainties are the discount rate, the years a cut counts, the chance the mission is achieved and Rethink's typical cuts; the next dollar counts at 49% of the past average (a stated funding gap for 2027-2031 and aid cuts, against surpluses in 2024 and 2025 mostly already signed to awardees). Every branch is discounted for missing data: no outcome of the work on the risk is measured, and most of the outbreak vaccines are not yet licensed and in use.

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

sections.title: Outcome

sections.title: Your dollar's share

Endemic branch: share of direct spending on the non-coronavirus priority pathogens
rows.explainer: Chikungunya, filoviruses, Lassa, mpox, Nipah and Rift Valley fever: about a third of direct spending. Shown for reading; the branch's cost share enters through end_year_share.

rows.label: Endemic branch: deaths a Lassa vaccine in use would avert a year

source.title: CEPI, Lassa fever (citing Smith et al. 2024, Health and economic impacts of Lassa vaccination campaigns in West Africa, Nature Medicine)
source.quote: CEPI-funded modelling suggests that introducing a safe and effective vaccine across 15 West African countries could save about 3,300 lives over 10 years

rows.explainer: 3,300 lives over ten years of a population-wide preventive campaign in West Africa's endemic districts, under the study's conservative efficacy assumption: 330 a year. The same study puts Lassa's burden at about 200,000 DALYs a year (2.0 million over ten years, 0.8 to 3.9 million), so better efficacy or wider use could avert more: 1,000 the high end; 100 the low end for reactive use only, which the study finds averts a tenth as much.

rows.label: Endemic branch: deaths a year from mpox
rows.explainer: WHO's situation report 67 (26 June 2026) counts 244 deaths among confirmed cases worldwide from January 2025 to May 2026, about 170 a year: the low end. Most cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo are never tested, so true deaths are likely several times the confirmed count: 500, our judgment, and up to 1,100 (about six and a half times the confirmed count) for a year with a larger untested epidemic.

rows.label: Endemic branch: deaths a year from filovirus, Nipah and Rift Valley fever outbreaks
rows.explainer: Today's outbreaks of the pathogens whose CEPI-funded vaccines are not yet licensed, averaged over years: filoviruses about 600 (the 2014-2016 West African Ebola epidemic's 11,000 deaths and later Ebola, Sudan and Marburg outbreaks, spread over the two decades since), Nipah and Rift Valley fever together about 200. MERS is left out: its spending is in the coronavirus line, which the endemic branch excludes. Our judgment, 300 to 3,000 (a large filovirus epidemic in the decade).

rows.label: Endemic branch: share of filovirus, Nipah, Rift Valley fever and mpox deaths vaccines in outbreak use would avert
rows.explainer: These vaccines would be used reactively, in rings and outbreak zones, after the first cases: the Lassa study finds reactive use averts a tenth of what preventive campaigns do, and Ebola ring vaccination (rVSV-ZEBOV) reached only part of each outbreak. 20%, our judgment, 5% to 50%.

rows.label: Endemic branch: chikungunya's yearly burden

source.title: de Roo et al. 2024, The global health and economic burden of chikungunya from 2011 to 2020, BMJ Global Health (Europe PMC abstract, PMC11624783)
source.quote: Our study revealed a total of 18.7 million chikungunya cases in 110 countries between 2011 and 2020, causing 1.95 million DALYs.

rows.explainer: 1.95 million DALYs over ten years: 195,000 a year, peaking in 2014-2016. The range is ours: the authors call it an underestimate (CEPI's page cites a Nature Medicine estimate of 35 million infections a year), and the 2025 outbreaks in China, the Indian Ocean and Europe were large; 100,000 for quieter years.

rows.label: Endemic branch: share of chikungunya's burden that is illness rather than deaths
rows.explainer: Only the illness part is counted, in DALYs; the few deaths are left out (a small understatement), so no death is valued here at another age mix than the site's. The study finds chronic illness the source of most DALYs ('Long-term chronic illness was the source of most costs and DALYs'): 80%, our judgment, 60% to 95%.

rows.label: Endemic branch: share of chikungunya's burden vaccines would avert
rows.explainer: Valneva's CEPI-funded vaccine is licensed (2023-2025 in the US, EU, UK, Canada and Brazil), but mostly for travellers and older adults in rich countries; the US licence was suspended in August 2025 after serious side effects in older people, and outbreaks are too unpredictable for routine campaigns in most endemic countries. 5%, our judgment, 1% to 20%.

rows.label: Endemic branch: chance the unlicensed vaccines (Lassa, filoviruses, Nipah, Rift Valley fever) are licensed and used
rows.explainer: Lassa, Nipah and Rift Valley fever candidates are in phase 1 or 2 (p. 4), and CEPI's filovirus work is on Sudan and Marburg viruses, which have no licensed vaccine. Vaccines against infectious diseases reach approval from phase 1 about a third of the time (Wong, Siah and Lo 2019, Biostatistics, the family's reference class); a vaccine for a disease of poor countries also needs a buyer, which Gavi and national programmes have yet to commit. 35%, our judgment, 15% to 70%.

rows.label: Endemic branch: chance the licensed vaccines (mpox, chikungunya) are used where the disease is
rows.explainer: The mpox (MVA-BN, LC16) and chikungunya (IXCHIQ, in Brazil, Canada, Europe and the UK, APR 2025 p. 15) vaccines CEPI funded trials of are licensed; what remains is uptake in endemic countries and, for children and older adults, the trials CEPI funds. 80%, our judgment, 50% to 100%.

rows.label: Endemic branch: years the field's funding brings the vaccines forward
rows.explainer: Without the money behind them, vaccines with no market (Lassa, Nipah, Rift Valley fever) would come years later or not at all; that someone else would do it later is this, not a counterfactual (Convention 5). Anchored on the research-returns class the medical-research family names: about 17 years from research to practice (Morris, Wooding and Grant 2011), of which funding at this scale plausibly brings a vaccine programme forward by about a third; 5 years, our judgment, 2 to 10; counted with the shared discount rate.

rows.label: Endemic branch: years until the unlicensed vaccines are in use
rows.explainer: From phase 2 to licensure, prequalification and campaigns: 5 years, our judgment, 2 to 10 (the cited Lassa page says only 'if it becomes licensed in the coming years'); discounted at the shared rate.

rows.label: Endemic branch: years until the licensed vaccines (mpox, chikungunya) are in use where the disease is
rows.explainer: These vaccines are licensed already; what remains is prequalification, trials in children and older adults, and procurement in endemic countries. 1 year, our judgment, 0 to 3; discounted at the shared rate.

source.title: CEPI, The 100 Days Mission (Imperial College London modelling for CEPI; Barnsley et al. 2024, Lancet Global Health)
source.quote: 8.3 million excess deaths could have been averted by the end of 2021

rows.explainer: Infectious disease modellers at Imperial College London, commissioned by CEPI: with safe and effective COVID-19 vaccines available by April 2020, within 100 days of the genome sequence, 8.3 million excess deaths could have been averted by the end of 2021.

rows.label: 100 Days Mission: share of a COVID-scale pandemic's deaths it would avert
rows.explainer: 8.3 million of COVID-19's 14.9 million excess deaths (the shared WHO figure): about {{row:mission_deaths_share}}. Read as the mission's cut in a pandemic's deaths; a faster or engineered pathogen would leave less time, which is in mission_p_achieved's low end.

rows.label: 100 Days Mission: chance it is achieved for the next pandemic
rows.explainer: No published forecast exists. COVID-19's first vaccines took 326 days (cepi.net/100-days-mission); in 2025 most 100 Days Mission tools were still in development (13 platform candidates, vaccine libraries for three of the viral families, regulatory reliance pilots: CEPI's 2025 board report, pp. 5-6), and a novel virus outside the libraries' families, a fast-spreading engineered pathogen or a failed trial would miss the target. 30%, our judgment, 10% to 60%.

rows.label: 100 Days Mission: funders' spending on it a year (CEPI and others, without developers' own money)
rows.explainer: Anchored on CEPI's own plan, US$3.6 billion for 2027-2031 ('The full CEPI 3.0 strategy requires US$3.6 billion', cepi.net/investors), $720M a year, plus other public and philanthropic funders of the mission's vaccine, regulatory and manufacturing work (BARDA's and the EU's HERA's rapid-response vaccine programmes, the Gates Foundation, Wellcome, national institutes), which we put at about half as much again (no published total of the mission's funding exists): $1.05B a year, our judgment, $0.7B (CEPI's own spending and little else) to $2.1B (others twice CEPI). The developers' co-investment is left out: bio_attribution_share counts it.

rows.label: 100 Days Mission: years of that spending until the capability is built
rows.explainer: The mission was set in 2021 and CEPI's two strategies run to 2031: about ten years of the effort's spending until the capability stands, our judgment, 5 to 15.

rows.label: Pandemic work: a typical project's cut per dollar at CEPI's size
rows.explainer: Rethink Priorities' typical pandemic projects cost $0.5-30M; at their rate one year of CEPI ($449M) would cut a catastrophic pandemic's yearly risk by about 10%. So a dollar at CEPI's size is measured by the 100 Days Mission it serves: the mission's cut in a pandemic's deaths (mission_deaths_share × mission_p_achieved) against what the typical rate implies for the mission's funders' dollars (mission_effort_per_year × mission_effort_years × the shared catastrophe cut per $1M), capped at 1. About 0.07. In the catastrophe-size and COVID-scale parts the step cancels the shared typical cut; the extinction part keeps Rethink's ratio of the extinction cut to the catastrophe cut, so the result moves with that ratio (up with the extinction cut, down with the catastrophe cut), not with the typical cut's level.
